author: Icedroid

comments.body: Because 3FS supports the coexistence of multiple replica counts, we cannot definitively determine the exact number of replicas. Therefore, when calculating total disk space usage, the system aggregates storage consumption without considering replica configurations. For instance, a 1MiB file with 2 replicas would be reported as occupying 2MiB of disk space in this statistical method.

title: How to scale up a 3FS cluster
body:
Thanks for this awesome project. We have successfully deployed a small-scale experimental cluster on Alibaba Cloud.

Now I want to test how it scales up. But there seems to be no document about how to add additional storage node to the cluster.

Here is my guess based on the very rough understanding to 3FS:

Option 1: I see there is a `Layout-ChainTableVersion` field in the output of `stat --display-layout`. So, it seems we can create a completely disjoint chain table and upload it to the cluster as version 2, which covers both old and new nodes. But it seems we cannot migrate existing data to the new version transparently.

Option 2: Maybe we can gradually move the existing chain. By adding an additional target to a chain to allow it to sync data, then remove one of the old targets from the chain. But the number of chains is fixed. As we add more nodes, we will need more chains to distribute the data. Can we somehow split an existing chain into two? Like the placement group of CEPH.

How do you scale up the cluster in DeepSeek?

Thanks again!
author: huww98

comments.body: In fact, we are using both Option 1 and Option 2.
Can you elaborate on how to scale up clusters when node reach the sdd capacity threshold?

From my guess:

When adding new node, we can add new then remove old target from chains, with `update-chain` command. If we don't have enough chains to keep nodes balanced, we need to create a new ChainTable with more chains (maybe 4x of the old one, from the experience of ceph pg). Then move all the data once to refresh the layout of existing files, maybe just `cp` and `rm` with fuse client.

Note that the migration to new ChainTable seems not transparent to user. e.g. If the user writes to the old file while we are copying it, the changes may be lost. I'm not satisfied with this, but I cannot come up with an easy solution. 3FS picks a subset of chain table for each file, which means we cannot just split a chain into two without change the stripe-size of each file. In contrast, ceph spread the data of every file in the whole pool.

Besides, it seems we cannot remove chains/targets even if we have migrated all the files in it. This is frustrating.

title: Why does create op need to be added in batcheop?
body: In my view, batch could be useful in occasion of concurrent setattr, to avoid foundation 'lock'. But how could create relative to this?
author: z47z

comments.body:
For each file, 3FS selects chains from the chain table in a round-robin manner to store the file's data. By default, the counter used for round-robin selection is maintained by the meta server.

There is an optional feature (disabled by default and rarely used) where each directory maintains its own separate counter, which can be beneficial in certain scenarios. For example, when you plan to store a large amount of data in one directory and want the data to be distributed across all storage servers as evenly as possible, maintaining a separate round-robin counter for this directory might achieve better distribution than using the global counter. To reduce transaction conflicts caused by counter modification operations, we have chosen to include the create operation in the batchOp as well.

The training input and the KVCache for inference are often read in the background when the previous batch is still being computed. The GPU memory is already loaded at the moment, so directly transferring into it is not very useful.
